newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND, MAY 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND, MAY 29.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Thursday.
- A Fianna Fail parliamentarian, Dan Wallace, broke ranks with the opposition party and demanded new laws banning abrotion.
- A clear majority of voters want new laws to reduce the soaring number of foreign refugees arriving in Ireland, according to an IMS poll.
- The Ryan family looks set to pull in almost $40 million when Ryanair shares begin to deal in the U.S. later today.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton will call for an immediate IRA ceasefire and support Sinn Fein's entry into all-party peace talks when he visits Britain today.
- Fianna Fail's Dan Wallace has broken party ranks and called for laws to outlaw abortion in Ireland.
- Ryanair shares will be floated on the Irish market at 195 Irish pence, the companyis expected to announce this afternoon.
- Fianna Fail leader Bertie Ahern has shied away from the offer of a debate with Prime Minister John Bruton ahead of the June 6 election.
- Helath workers last night overwhelmingly accepted a 10 million irish pound Labour Court award giving them pay rises of up to 3,000 pounds.
- U.S.singer Bob Dylan has pulled out of a weekend concert in Cork because of heart illness.
